confirmed.title: Reveal's 15s auto-advance is only cancelled by taps on [data-action] controls; taps on the card/verdict are ignored, and the one cancelling tap (a vote chip) flips the recorded vote
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=555 as a fresh visitor (empty localStorage), fast flow on (default)
New game -> Skip photo on every row -> Shuffle & start
On the pass screen tap the continue button (card draws, song starts)
Tap any gap, tap Place here
On the reveal, while the Next player button shows its draining fill (~3s in), tap the revealed card face (#reveal-flip) or the verdict banner - not a button
Wait out the remaining ~12s: the app auto-advances to the pass screen anyway

Variant (seed 44004, Advanced mode, vote both chips first): tapping a vote chip to 'pause' does cancel-and-rearm, but the group's recorded vote flips (banner changes from 'Correct. The card is yours.' to 'Right spot, but you had to name it too.')
confirmed.expected: Per the shipped fast-flow contract ('any other interaction cancels the countdown'), any tap on the reveal cancels the auto-advance without side effects, and the screen stays until Next player is tapped.
confirmed.actual: Only clicks landing on a [data-action] control cancel (ui.js global click handler ~4428); taps on the card face, year, artist, artwork, banner, or reveal strip leave the countdown draining and the screen self-advances at 15s - and the only non-Next controls that do cancel are the vote chips, whose tap mutates the vote and immediately re-arms a fresh countdown.
sources: adv-expert:Reveal auto-advance countdown is not cancelled by taps anywhere except the two vote chips, and a chip tap silently flips the group's vote
chaos:Reveal's 15s auto-advance is not cancelled by taps on the revealed card or verdict - only button taps cancel it
confirmed.rationale: Two independent testers (seeds 44004 and 555/4441, different areas) hit the identical root defect: the cancel logic lives only in the click handler's [data-action] branch, so non-control taps never cancel. The vote-chip flip is a corollary of the same root (the only cancelling non-Next controls are stateful toggles), so it is one cluster, not two. Severity S3, not S2: no control is broken or unreachable - Next player and the chips work, the auto-advance is the fast-flow feature itself, and the flow is janky-but-recoverable (the vote flip is user-initiated on a visible toggle whose banner updates immediately). It is a broken interaction promise mid-argument, not a dead feature, and not a wrong game-rule outcome computed by the app.

v1.reason: Reproduced both legs exactly as written on the live site in fresh browser sessions. Part A (seed 555, classic): with the reveal countdown armed, real locator clicks at +3s on #reveal-flip and #verdict-banner left data-autonext="true" and the app auto-advanced to the pass screen 15241ms after the reveal — taps on non-control surfaces neither cancel nor reset the timer. Part B (seed 44004, advanced, correct placement, both chips voted): banner read "Correct. The card is yours."; a +3s tap on the Title chip flipped confirmations.title to false, banner became "Right spot, but you had to name it too.", and the countdown re-armed (advance fired 15181ms after the chip tap), after which the correctly placed card was discarded — matching the finding's quoted strings verbatim. Code corroborates the root cause: ui.js's armAutoNext doc (lines 1930-1937) promises "ANY other interaction on the screen cancels the timer", but the only cancel lives in onClick's [data-action] branch (~4429) behind an early return at 4413, so card/banner/strip taps never reach it. Not by-design (brief's list doesn't cover it; the shipped comment states the opposite intent) and not exaggerated: severity stays S3 per the rubric — janky-but-recoverable flow, no control broken or hidden, and the vote flip is a user-initiated toggle whose banner updates immediately (engine outcome matches the recorded vote, so no S1 wrong-rule outcome; no dead feature, so no S2). Evidence: scratch/qa/round-4/verify-reveal-autonext-cancel-only-on-control-taps-1/ (verify.mjs + 5 screenshots).

confirmed.title: Fast-flow auto-advance countdown has no text/ARIA equivalent, disappears entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, and Tab navigation does not cancel it
repro: Fresh page: https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=555 (fast flow on by default)
New game -> Skip photo on every row -> Shuffle & start -> tap #btn-pass-continue
Place the card on any gap -> Place here; reveal appears with #btn-next-player carrying data-autonext='true'
Inspect #btn-next-player: no aria-label, title, aria-describedby, or live-region text mentions the countdown - the only indication is the animated ::before fill
Press Tab and wait 15s: the countdown is not cancelled; phase flips to 'turn-start' and focus is yanked to #pass-title
Repeat with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: the fill is display:none (app.css ~2949) with no replacement, so the reveal auto-advances with zero visible or audible warning
confirmed.expected: The 15s auto-advance is perceivable without animation (text/aria equivalent or live-region note), and keyboard interaction counts as an interaction that cancels it.
confirmed.actual: The countdown exists only as a visual ::before drain (removed entirely under reduced motion) with no ARIA or text equivalent; Tab/arrow keys never cancel (cancel fires only on data-action clicks), so the verdict screen is replaced under a screen-reader, keyboard, or reduced-motion user with no warning.
sources: a11y:Fast-flow reveal auto-advance has no accessible or reduced-motion indication and keyboard navigation does not cancel it
confirmed.rationale: Kept separate from the cancel-scope cluster: although the Tab-does-not-cancel aspect shares that root cause, the core defect here is distinct and needs a different fix - the countdown has no non-visual representation at all, and reduced-motion strips its only indicator. Severity S3 per the rubric's 'minor a11y' line: no focus trap and no unreachable control (a keyboard user activating any control via Enter fires a click and cancels; mouse/touch users are unaffected), and the game continues. Borderline S2 - a timed context change with zero perceivable warning is a WCAG 2.2.1 failure that costs affected users the verdict and any claim window every turn - so verification should check whether fast flow can be disabled in settings; if it cannot, S2 becomes defensible.

v1.reason: Reproduced live (seed 555) exactly as written. On the reveal, #btn-next-player carries data-autonext='true' with no aria-label, title, aria-describedby, or live-region text mentioning the 15s countdown (live-status said only "Player 1's turn..."); the sole indicator is the ::before autonext-drain animation (app.css:2929-2943). A real Tab press did not cancel (cancel only fires in the click dispatcher, ui.js:4429; onKeydown has no cancel path), and 16s later the screen flipped to pass/turn-start with focus yanked to #pass-title. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the ::before is display:none (app.css:2949-2951) while the JS timer still runs — the reveal auto-advanced after 15s with zero visible indication (screenshot shows a plain button). Not by-design per the brief's list, and the code's own stated intent ("ANY other interaction cancels"; reduced-motion loses "nothing that carries meaning") is contradicted. Severity stays S3, not S2: I verified both mitigations the finding's rationale made decisive — fast flow CAN be disabled through the visible UI (menu toggle; next reveal had no data-autonext and never advanced), and keyboard activation (Enter on a focused data-action control) does cancel the countdown, so there is no trap or unreachable control and the flow is recoverable. Fits the rubric's "minor a11y" line. Evidence in scratch/qa/round-4/verify-reveal-autonext-no-accessible-indication-1/ (verify.mjs, verify-toggle.mjs, 5 screenshots).

confirmed.title: Challenge lock pills render in the active player's seat colour instead of each challenger's own colour
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/index.html?debug=1&seed=101 (fresh localStorage)
New game -> remove the 4th player row, name rows Ann/Ben/Cat, tap Skip photo on each row -> Shuffle & start
On Ann's pass screen, tap the pass hero (fast flow draws the card)
Tap 'Challenge · 1 token' -> pick Ben -> tap any gap in his timeline -> 'Lock in — spend 1 token'
Tap 'Challenge · 1 token' again -> pick Cat -> tap any gap -> Lock in
Inspect the 'Ben challenged' / 'Cat challenged' pills above the Place here button: both are Ann's teal rgb(12,133,153) instead of Ben's #f08c00 and Cat's #7048e8
confirmed.expected: Each pill wears the challenger's own seat colour, per the markup's own contract comment (index.html:1001) and the .lock CSS built on var(--seat).
confirmed.actual: The renderer (ui.js ~2940-2952) fills the label text but never applies the challenger's colour, so --seat is inherited from the active player's screen theming and every pill renders in the active player's colour.
sources: tokens-bets:Challenge lock pills render in the active player's colour, not the challenger's own colour
confirmed.rationale: Real cosmetic defect contradicting the app's own colour-identity convention, but the pill text ('Ben challenged') carries the correct information, so nothing is actually mislabelled - only the colour cue is inconsistent. That is the rubric's S4 'subtle inconsistency', matching the reporter's own proposal; S3 'misleading' would require the identity information itself to be wrong or absent.

v1.reason: Reproduced live in my own fresh browser session following the repro verbatim (seed=101, Ann/Ben/Cat, fast-flow draw via pass hero, two challenges locked via the sheet UI). Both 'Ben challenged' and 'Cat challenged' pills computed background rgb(12,133,153) = Ann's #0c8599 teal, not Ben's #f08c00 or Cat's #7048e8; neither li had an inline --seat, so they inherit the active player's colour published on document.body (ui.js:3865). Source confirms the mechanism: index.html:1001 and the tpl-challenge-lock comment (index.html:1516-1518) demand the challenger's own colour via per-li --seat, .lock CSS (app.css:2009) is built on var(--seat), and the renderer (ui.js ~2939-2952) only fills the label. Not in the by-design list and contradicts the app's own contract comments, so it is a real defect — but the pill text names the challenger correctly, so only the colour cue is inconsistent: rubric S4 'subtle inconsistency', matching the proposal. Evidence in scratch/qa/round-4/verify-challenge-lock-pills-active-player-color-1/ (verify.mjs, 07-pills-final.png, 08-locks-closeup.png).

confirmed.title: Deck holds the same song twice: 'Puff, the Magic Dragon' (1963) exists under two ids differing only by '&' vs 'and' in the artist slug
repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/deck.js (byte-identical to repo public/music/deck.js)
Search for 'puff-the-magic-dragon'

Two entries exist: id 'peter-paul-mary-puff-the-magic-dragon' (artist 'Peter, Paul & Mary') and id 'peter-paul-and-mary-puff-the-magic-dragon' (artist 'Peter, Paul and Mary'), both title 'Puff, the Magic Dragon', year 1963 - the only duplicate pair in a normalized scan of all 1186 entries
Both cards are independently drawable in the same game (each has its own previews.json entry pointing at the identical iTunes preview URL); one was drawn live in session 3
confirmed.expected: Every one of the advertised 1186 deck cards is a distinct song; no song can be drawn twice in one game.
confirmed.actual: The 1186-card deck holds 1185 distinct songs; the identical 1963 recording is two separately drawable cards.
sources: classic-game:Deck contains the same song twice: "Puff, the Magic Dragon" (1963) appears under two ids
confirmed.rationale: Genuine content defect, not by-design, with solid evidence (normalized scan, live-fetched file identical to repo). S4: a single duplicate in 1186 cards is a subtle data inconsistency - both draws produce a legal, correctly-judged turn with the correct year, so no game-rule outcome is wrong; the worst case (same song twice in one night, second naming attempt trivial) is rare polish-level impact.

v1.reason: Reproduced end to end. Live deck.js is byte-identical to repo public/music/deck.js (sha256 match), and a real Chromium session importing /deck.js from the live origin shows both entries: id 'peter-paul-mary-puff-the-magic-dragon' ("Peter, Paul & Mary") and id 'peter-paul-and-mary-puff-the-magic-dragon' ("Peter, Paul and Mary"), both "Puff, the Magic Dragon", 1963 (deck.js lines 118-119). My own normalized artist+title scan confirms exactly the claimed numbers: 1186 entries, one duplicate group, 1185 distinct songs. Both ids exist in previews.json with the identical iTunes preview URL, and engine.js normaliseDeck() performs no dedupe, so both cards are independently drawable in one game. The live home screen literally advertises "1186 songs · 1950–2025". Not on the by-design list. Severity stays S4: both draws produce a legal, correctly-judged turn with the correct year, so no game-rule outcome is wrong — worst case is the same song playing twice in one night, a polish-level content inconsistency.

coverage.coverage: First run & home screen on the LIVE site (music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app), ~18 min across 9 Playwright sessions under scratch/qa/round-4/first-run/. Tested: fresh-visitor first paint (clean context, empty localStorage) with resume card correctly absent; home at 320x568, 360x740, 393x852, 768x1024, 1450x1100, 2000x1450 (zero horizontal overflow everywhere, controls never hidden); How-to-play rules read end to end word by word against the brief's rules (token costs -1/+1/-3, four modes, targets 5/10/15, co-op shared pool 6 and mistake limit 3, challenge small print, streak bonus, buy-in-never-charges) plus rules layout on mobile and 1450x1100 — no typos or wrong rule statements found; manifest.json (200, sane name/start_url/display/theme colors), icon.svg + apple-touch-icon.png (200), service worker registered and active, second visit renders; resume behaviour — saved a game mid-turn (card drawn AND gap selected, seed 777), reloaded, resume card appeared with accurate detail line, and after resuming EVERY field matched (players, tokens, per-player timelines, deck count 1181, mode, drawn card, selected gap, phase); ended-game state swaps the home card to "See final result / Game over" and reopens the recap; menu sheet (exists only on the play screen; home/setup/pass/reveal intentionally have none) — every row exercised: Scoreboard opens standings with correct deck/token counts and "Back to the game" returns to play; How to play opens/closes back to play; Fast flow, Skip pass-the-phone, Sound, Reduce motion all flip, persist to localStorage and survive reload, and skip-pass+fast-flow-off actually changed the flow (pass screen skipped, no auto-draw); "Play songs with" select is tappable, keyboard-operable, persists, and switches the play screen to Spotify QR mode; "Home — the game stays saved" keeps the resume card; End game uses an armed confirm ("Tap again to end the game") and a level early end crowns nobody ("Level when it ended: ... 1 card each"); done/scrim/Escape close the menu with focus returned to the menu button; Tab reaches and Enter operates the menu and all sheet close buttons. Console/pageerror monitored in every session: zero errors total. Investigated and REJECTED as non-findings: Escape not closing rules/scoreboard (full screens, not dialogs; close buttons keyboard-reachable; the menu dialog does close on Escape), a 0x0 select (my probe hit the hidden setup screen's #playback-source; the menu's #opt-playback-source works fine), sticky setup footer appearing to cover the Classic mode card (fullPage-screenshot artifact only — real scroll positions render correctly), and desktop home whitespace (deliberate centered composition, nothing hidden). Ran out of time for: deep offline-mode behaviour, real photo upload on setup, and forget-person on a roster with saved photos (no forget affordance exists for initial-only rosters).

Tested the live site (https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app) at 393x852 across five fresh browser sessions driven only through the visible UI (Playwright scripts in /home/user/fabians-red-card/scratch/qa/round-4/roster/, ~25 screenshots there, all reviewed). Covered and found correct: (1) Bounds 2-8 enforced honestly - remove disabled at 2 with reason 'At least two players', Add disabled at 8 with 'Eight players is the maximum', count note tracks exactly, force-clicks do nothing, placeholder names reuse the lowest free 'Player N' so removes+adds never mint duplicates. (2) Photo gating - Start disabled with live honest copy that switches singular/plural ('One player still needs a photo - or tap Skip photo for them' / 'N players still need...'), clears when all rows have photo or skip; Skip photo chip toggles text (Skip photo/Photo skipped) and aria-pressed; status line honest (Photo needed/Photo added/Using their initial). (3) Names - 40-char input clips at maxlength 16 with a visible 16/16 countdown; emoji name (guitar emoji + diacritics) survives through state, pass hero, play topbar and standings with no overflow; whitespace-only name falls back to 'Player N' at start; duplicate names are allowed but visibly flagged with a dashed underline and both players start fine with distinct seat colours.
